decisions.reason: This automation module fits the firm's core move toward digitally optimized and energy-efficient infrastructure operation, so after remaining in the portfolio it is more likely to be integrated further than withdrawn.

The web tool supports planners and can help generate project business, but as a relatively light standalone software offering outside the firm's heavier installed-system core it still has the highest rationalization risk.

The fouling detection system remains close to the firm's established combination of machinery, monitoring, and operational transparency, though there is some chance it could later be folded into a broader package.

The spring-controlled flap weir is strategically adjacent to the firm's water-control business and useful in project solutions, but as a newer mechanical niche product it carries a moderate portfolio-pruning risk.

An energy management system for water facilities directly matches the firm's stated direction toward networked, efficient, and environmentally focused infrastructure control, making continuation very likely.
The overflow flap gate line fits the firm's flood-control and water-level-regulation offering well, and a dedicated product-line presentation suggests commercial commitment rather than an early exit.
